item.title: UAE's Ras Al Khaimah, Sharjah reopen several beaches after tanker oil spill
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Authorities in the United Arab Emirates' Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah emirates said they had reopened several beaches following closures prompted by an oil spill from a tanker damaged in a suspected attack in the Gulf last month.

Sharjah's media office said the beaches had reopened after authorities brought pollution caused by the spill under control.

"The relevant authorities confirm that the emirate's beaches and marine environment are safe, allowing the public to visit and enjoy various marine activities safely," it said.

item.title: Wizz Air chief calls for Europe-wide coordination on bomb threats
item.description:
By Gianluca Lo Nostro and Yamini Kalia

Nov 12 (Reuters) - Europe needs a more harmonised approach to security and a body to lead it against "hybrid warfare" following a recent series of bomb threats, the CEO of Hungarian budget airline Wizz Air said on Thursday.

Bomb threats have disrupted travel, newsrooms and schools across Europe in November, with the latest alert temporarily disrupting train services in northern France on Thursday morning.

item.title: Explainer-Can a new US Congress mean an end to the Iran war?
item.description:
By Patricia Zengerle

WASHINGTON, Nov 12 (Reuters) - The American public wants the unpopular eight-month-long war on Iran to end, and showed it by handing President Donald Trump's Republicans a resounding defeat in last week's congressional elections.

Trump acknowledged that unhappiness about the conflict contributed to his party's losses, but defends the war, both insisting that he has won itand saying it will continue.

Congress cannot unilaterally end the war, but can pressure the president to do so.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital deadliest since election
item.description:
An Israeli strike killed six people and wounded nearly 30 more in southern Gaza's Nasser hospital early Thursday, Gaza health officials said, the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month.

The Israeli military confirmed the attack, saying it targeted "a senior Hamas terrorist and additional terrorists from Hamas's military wing" it said were operating from the hospital, which it has long accused the Palestinian Islamist movement of using to shelter militants.

item.title: Venezuela tells COP31 it has a sovereign right to pump more oil
item.description:
By William James and Simon Jessop

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Venezuela’s Acting President Delcy Rodriguez told the COP31 climate conference on Thursday that the country has the sovereign right to develop its oil industry, even as it recognises the importance of combatting climate change.

Her comments at the UN talks on Turkey’s Mediterranean coast jar with efforts by other conference leaders to convince global governments to accelerate a shift from carbon-emitting fossil fuels.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Starshield speed limited again, hampering Ukraine's defences
item.description:
Nov 12 (Reuters) - President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Thursday that Ukrainian military units had recorded significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications service for several days, affecting the entire front line and Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

In a post on Telegram, Zelenskiy said that systemic restrictions were limiting the speed at which Starshield could be used to 161 kph (100 mph). Starshield is the military version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite communications service.

item.title: Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital kills six, Gaza civil defence says
item.description:
CAIRO, Nov 12 (Reuters) - An Israeli airstrike on a building at Nasser Hospitalinsouthern Gaza killed at least six people, including a surgeon, and wounded 20 others early on Thursday, a spokesman for Gaza's civil defence service told Reuters.

The Israeli military later said it had targeted a senior Hamas militant and other members of the group's armed wing who it said were operating inside the hospital in Khan Younis.

item.title: Motor racing-Hamilton urges Israel to let Gaza aid in after Rafah visit
item.description:
Nov 11 (Reuters) - Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.

Hamilton, a seven-times world champion, arrived in El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

item.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missiles, drones; group denies targeting Mecca
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi missiles and drones launched towards Riyadh, Mecca and other regions on Wednesday, as hostilities between the Iran-aligned group and the kingdom worsen.

The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Yemeni group said it had intercepted and destroyed three cruise missiles headed to the Riyadh region, two drones aimed at Mecca and southern areas and two missiles pointed towards the west.

item.title: Iran tells COP31 it wants compensation for environmental damage from US-Israeli strikes
item.description:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian told the COP31 climate conference on Wednesday his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, saying the issue related to global efforts to fight climate change.

"We expect the global communityto establish a genuine and meaningful link between climate commitments in times of peace and responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms," he said.
